Repository inspection and evidence boundary

Inspected 05 October 2026. Documentation baseline: game_docs/main at 0151e36ed08d779557fd35433c49688d50abdf15. Game checkout and remote main/HEAD: RPG at 038bded3706b9f0c0594f414975fe69f42738470. The tracked game tree contains only .gitignore; local Content, Intermediate and Saved directories contain no project files. No .uproject, Config, Source, Build.cs, Target.cs, plugins, C++ classes or .uasset/.umap files were available to inspect.

The GitHub connector could read game_docs but returned 404 for RPG. A successful read-only git ls-remote against the checkout’s configured SSH origin confirmed that remote main/HEAD matches the local initial commit. This is evidence of the available repository state, not proof that development assets do not exist elsewhere.

The documentation is an offline HTML build manual, with shared site/style.css and site/app.js, a local search index, 12 build phases, 19 system chapters, an original roadmap and a machine-readable 149-asset manifest. Its audit explicitly says these are plans/specifications, not generated or compiled assets. The asset names below are documented planned identities, not verified game implementations.

Engine target is the user’s Unreal Engine 5.8.3. Local installation /Users/Shared/Epic Games/UE_5.8 reports Build.version 5.8.3, changelist 58210709. Relevant engine headers/source were inspected for save API, lifecycle and movement constraints. Static source inspection does not prove project compilation or runtime behavior.

Before the first actual native implementation, inspect the developer’s complete .uproject, enabled plugins, Config, actual Blueprint parent chains/components/graphs, source targets and save fixtures. Reconcile differences into this page before relying on proposed native mappings. Do not manufacture a game project as part of this documentation task.

Project-specific ownership baseline

Documented owner / lifetimeAuthoritative responsibilityC++ adoption boundary
BP_GameInstance / sessionCreates/retains Profile and WorldState; coordinates coherent multi-owner commits, travel value handoff and save queue.A native GameInstance base retains the same narrow coordination. No attacks, AI, per-item math or world Actors as permanent truth.
BP_PlayerProfile / UObject session modelTotalXP, UnspentSkillPoints, PurchasedSkillIds, InventoryEntries and EquippedEntryIdsBySlot; derived level/build queries.Keep one Profile-owned inventory and slot map. No new inventory/equipment components merely because generic RPG examples use them.
BP_WorldState / UObject session modelPersistent object records/flags, active checkpoint, discovered areas/rooms and remembered NPC facts.Values and IDs; no direct calls to Profile, live doors or widgets.
BP_SaveGame / snapshotHeader, Character, World and derived Recovery values.Serialization container, not another authoritative session model.
BP_GameMode / current mapReadiness, persistent projection, one explicit player spawn, body setup and recovery orchestration.Per-map lifetime. Does not replace session persistence or ordinary travel policy.
BP_AreaRoot / current areaCurrent area/room and local camera context.Discovery commits to WorldState; local registry expires with the map.
BP_PlayerController / local input and UI contextInput routing, local widgets, current conversation cursor and modal policy.Requests commands, binds/pulls views and replaces body references. No inventory/skill rule copies.
BP_PlayerCharacter / current bodyMovement intent, buffer/coyote/jump budget, facing, composition and adapters.PaperCharacter base; inherited CharacterMovement owns floor/velocity integration.
BPC_Stats / bodyFinal calculated stat cache from complete inputs.Rebuild on relevant changes, not Tick. Does not mutate Profile or Health.
BPC_Health / bodyCurrent health, accepted damage/restoration and lethal detection.Queries Stats capacity/defense; broadcasts complete facts; no rewards, saving or checkpoint knowledge.
BPC_ActionState + BPC_Combat / bodyExclusive action/token and local attack phase/execution respectively.One lock owner; stale execution cannot release another action.
BPC_Abilities + BP_AbilityBase / body and executionDerived unlock cache, charges/recharge; one accepted executor.Custom existing ability architecture; no automatic GAS migration or added resource system.
BPC_StatusEffects / bodyTimed effect handles/expiry and modifier sources.Refresh duration without magnitude stacking under baseline; not permanent stat mutation.
BPC_Interaction / bodyCandidate selection and revalidated interface command.No cast switch for every target type or world-wide per-frame search.
BPC_PersistentState / placed ActorIdentity/readiness and projection of a WorldState record.Actor is replaceable; record is authority. Applying a saved completion is not legitimate death/reward.
BP_EnemyAIController + BP_EnemyBaseTarget/decision state versus body execution/death adapter.AI requests Combat; no second attack timeline. Unique completion uses coherent session reward operation.
BPC_FlipbookAnimator / body presentationVisual state, shared clock and synchronized equipment layers.Observes gameplay; no hit/reward authority or skeletal AnimInstance assumption.
BP_NPCBase + dialogue definitionsInteractable world participant and authored dialogue variants/conditions.Controller owns cursor, WorldState owns memory; no hostile-enemy inheritance.

The authoritative source for the documented ownership is State ownership and Architecture. These engineering boundaries preserve it. Native types such as UPlayerProfile, UHealthComponent or EActionState are proposed counterparts used in examples, not an existing source inventory.

Movement architecture

Preserve side-scrolling X/Z movement with Y-plane constraint, capsule physics, Paper2D flipbook visuals and native CharacterMovement integration. The body supplies one intent path; controller clears completed/canceled input. Do not multiply AddMovementInput’s scale by DeltaSeconds or apply intent from both input and Tick.

One jump policy owns buffering, coyote permission, committed jump budget and one variable-height cut. Actual floor/mode observations gate rearming. Do not create a parallel physics simulation or fallback native Jump path that doubles the deliberate launch.

LaunchCharacter stores a pending launch processed by movement later, so immediate positive Z velocity cannot be assumed. OnLanded still reports Falling; confirm the subsequent movement mode before rearming. These mechanics are verified against LaunchCharacter and OnLanded. Post-movement observation ordering must still be proven in the actual game.

Pending cut after a released buffered press must produce a short jump without cutting falling velocity, applying repeated cuts or creating a new impulse after a ceiling. Keep native movement mode, action state and visual state separate. Movement tuning is independent of RPG level absent a deliberate design change. See movement policy/tests.

Combat, abilities and effects

ActionState owns permission and execution token. Combat owns None/Windup/Active/Recovery and the authoritative damage timing; animator observes. At a hitch, process active interval crossing even if the next elapsed time has already entered recovery. Spatial sweeps/blocking geometry must also be checked; clock coverage alone does not guarantee a hit.

Record each target attempt before calling its Damageable adapter. The existing baseline counts a rejected invulnerability attempt once per swing. Health accepts damage/mitigation once and establishes lethal state before callbacks. Body adapters interrupt/knock back/recover; enemy adapters request legitimate rewards. Ranged active entry spawns one projectile instead of also executing melee damage. Missing animation affects no rule.

Abilities derive unlocks from Profile purchases, validate/load before acceptance, initialize an inert executor and spend charge only after successful preparation/spawn. Accepted interruption/miss does not refund the baseline cost. Effects refresh the same EffectId’s duration without stacking magnitude. Runtime Actor-containing DamageSpec/AbilityContext values cannot enter snapshots or travel handoffs. See combat, abilities and effects.

Stats, inventory, equipment, progression and skills

Profile is persistent character truth. Owned EntryIds and equipment slot references stay coherent under validated operations; all stacking is centralized. Stats is a body cache, rebuilt from Profile/definitions plus current temporary effects. UI does not trigger required rebuilds. Capacity increases cannot become free healing.

TotalXP is stored; level is derived from the validated versioned curve. Award all crossed threshold points once on an XP award; import recomputes without awards. Skill availability is one derived query reused at purchase commit. Purchases, point deduction, exclusions and prerequisites are atomic inside Profile. Ability grants are derived, not another independently saved unlock list. See the existing inventory, equipment, stats, progression and skills chapters.

World, interaction, NPCs and saving

The world uses interconnected ordinary area maps with rooms/backtracking, not an assumed World Partition/seamless-world redesign. Persistent world records survive replaceable Actors. GameMode activates projected Actors/player only after readiness; the old body stops before value handoff capture. Checkpoints select recovery location without rolling progression back.

Interaction queries do not mutate world facts; targets revalidate a request and route it to the correct owner. NPC conditions are read-only; only authored conversation completion commits remembered flags. Modal conversation pauses simulation under the existing policy. Disk load restores persistent values and clean runtime recovery, not an exact dialogue cursor or enemy position. See world bootstrap, persistent projection, interaction, NPCs/dialogue and save-safe engineering.

Documented type inventory

All 149 names, parents, folders, phases and asset instances remain in the existing asset register. The register contains 29 ordinary Blueprint Classes, 9 Actor Components, 11 schema classes, 11 enums, 23 structs, 4 interfaces, 1 function library, 23 data instances, 1 table, 10 widgets, 12 input assets, 5 maps and 10 art/animation assets. No native project module organization has yet been established.

Blueprint Actor Component

BPC_ActionState, BPC_FlipbookAnimator, BPC_Stats, BPC_Health, BPC_Combat, BPC_Interaction, BPC_PersistentState, BPC_Abilities, BPC_StatusEffects.

Blueprint Enumeration

E_ActionState, E_AnimState, E_StatId, E_AttackPhase, E_CombatSide, E_EquipmentSlot, E_EntryReason, E_ItemKind, E_EnemyBrainState, E_SkillAvailability, E_ConditionKind.

Blueprint Structure

S_AnimationSnapshot, S_StatBlock, S_StatModifier, S_DamageSpec, S_DamageResult, S_InventoryEntry, S_CharacterSave, S_WorldObjectRecord, S_CheckpointState, S_WorldSave, S_RecoveryData, S_TransitionRequest, S_RuntimeTravelState, S_SaveHeader, S_ItemGrant, S_Reward, S_LevelProgressionRow, S_AbilityRuntimeState, S_ActiveEffect, S_AbilityContext, S_Condition, S_DialogueLine, S_DialogueVariant.

Blueprint Interface

BPI_Damageable, BPI_Interactable, BPI_PersistentActor, BPI_AbilityTarget.

Blueprint Class — data schema

BPDA_AnimationSet, BPDA_CharacterDefinition, BPDA_AttackDefinition, BPDA_GameCatalog, BPDA_AreaDefinition, BPDA_ItemDefinition, BPDA_EnemyDefinition, BPDA_SkillDefinition, BPDA_AbilityDefinition, BPDA_EffectDefinition, BPDA_DialogueDefinition.

Ordinary classes include GameInstance/GameModes, PlayerController/PlayerCharacter/Profile, WorldState/SaveGame, AreaRoot/SpawnPoint/RoomVolume/AreaTransition, InteractableBase with Checkpoint/Switch/Door/Pickup, NPCBase, EnemyBase with melee/ranged children and EnemyAIController, Hazard/ProjectileBase/AbilityBase, plus development fixtures. Their documented native bases remain GameInstance, GameModeBase, PlayerController, UObject, USaveGame, APaperCharacter, Actor, PlayerStart and AIController. APaperCharacter’s flipbook visual differs from the ordinary Character skeletal Mesh setup: Epic APaperCharacter.

Existing Content naming is intentional: BP_ classes, BPC_ components, BPDA_ schemas, DA_ instances, BPI_ contracts, E_/S_ value assets, WBP_ widgets, IA_/IMC_ input, DT_ table, L_ maps and T_/SPR_/FB_ visuals. Preserve the 20 Content folders and development fixture placements; source directories need not mirror every content folder. Gameplay tags/capability IDs remain the existing semantic vocabulary, not permission for new traversal.

Conflicts and a scoped migration path

Observed/documented issueRequired treatment
No game implementation is available.There are no verified code violations to list. Acquire/inspect the complete project before claiming implementation conformity or beginning migration.
The older guide is Blueprint-first and says its C++ reference requires no migration.Historical recipes remain usable for their existing scope. New/modified C++ follows this standard; stable rules migrate only with requested feature work. One authoritative path survives each migration.
The asset register describes Blueprint enums/structs/interfaces, whereas examples show native types.Native reflection creates different type identities. Inventory consumers, convert/reparent one cohesive feature, preserve values, compile assets and test fixtures. Do not assume spelling/ordinals or redirects guarantee automatic conversion.
Source API/data aliases disagree.Keep canonical single implementations/stores documented in Architecture Notes; optional wrappers delegate. Do not rename all consumers during unrelated work.
Cross-model deferred notification helpers are not fully implemented in the plan.Define narrow native internal staging/commit access during that feature. Do not make all state/public mutators Blueprint-accessible to resolve visibility.
E_ActionState includes Ability; E_AnimState has no Ability entry.Preserve the documented Attack cosmetic fallback until an explicit presentation decision; do not add a new gameplay state or traversal feature.
Ranged hook, mandatory save failure and lab setup have documented gaps.Resolve the concrete hook/failure/harness during its scoped implementation and validate it; no extra manager, area asset or speculative enum is implied.
Blueprint-owned component may become a native default subobject.Inspect the actual asset, remove competing instances/graph rule paths in the same migration and verify serialized defaults/override assignments.

Suggested order when native implementation is actually requested: establish the real module/toolchain; select the current feature; stabilize its contract/value types; implement its owner in .cpp; retain configured Blueprint composition; adapt callers; remove the competing rule path; run build/UHT, Blueprint and domain tests; test saves when affected. This is a migration method, not a request to port all 149 planned assets at once.

The canonical original roadmap and manifest remain unchanged. This standard changes engineering guidance, not gameplay design. It does not approve multiplayer, GAS, a quest/faction framework, rarity systems, respec, mana, extra traversal or a universal game manager.
